
Two arXiv papers from the RSS scout directly address tool-use design and optimization in agentic systems with empirical or framework grounding. Grok social signals were deprioritized due to unverifiable URLs. The top two candidates both meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with strong relevance to production agentic workflow design.

## Suggestions

- [To Call or Not to Call: A Framework to Assess and Optimize LLM Tool Calling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00737) — Presents a framework for assessing and optimizing when LLM agents invoke tools, directly addressing tool-use decision design across the agent execution lifecycle.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)

- [Are Tools All We Need? Unveiling the Tool-Use Tax in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00136) — Empirically characterizes the overhead and tradeoffs of tool use in LLM agents, providing grounding for architectural decisions about tool integration in agentic workflows.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability)
